profile.name: Paulina Murzanska
profile.headline: React Front-end Developer · AI-augmented development
profile.summary: React front-end developer with 5+ years building with React, Next.js, TypeScript and Vue, 4+ of them in commercial client teams, often on several client projects in parallel. Every project needs something different, so I adapt fast, spot the gaps nobody owns and fill them: a documentation app covering 5 applications and 15 releases that replaced scattered SharePoint files, a proper SPA architecture for a struggling Vue app as Lead Front-end in a team of 6, a self-service test runner for non-technical users, and a rescue of an AI-generated app that didn't work. I work AI-augmented, with agents assisting me from Jira ticket to docs and my review on every change.

whyMe.proof: Vue, Shopify, NetSuite: productive in days
Built docs for 5 apps nobody had documented
5+ years with React, Next.js, TypeScript, Vue
Agents from ticket to PR, docs on Karpathy's LLM Wiki

bestFit: Product teams that want ownership, not just tickets
E-commerce on Shopify or headless commerce
ERP and NetSuite projects that need a real front end
Software houses and consultancies with changing clients
Lead or senior-track roles with client contact

services.title: Build front-end features
services.description: Production UI in React, Next.js, TypeScript and Vue: components, routing, state management, API integration, performance and SEO. Shipped for e-commerce, ERP, education and insurance products.

services.title: Fix and structure what's broken
services.description: I step into apps that grew the wrong way, whether a Vue app built as one page or an AI-generated app built by a non-technical client, and give them a working architecture: proper SPA structure, routing and clean component patterns.

services.title: Fill the gaps nobody owns
services.description: If something slows the team down, I build the fix. Scattered SharePoint documents became a documentation app covering 5 applications and 15 releases. A terminal-only test suite became a web app that non-technical users run themselves.

services.title: Ship with quality built in
services.description: QA experience means I test like a user and fix like a developer: Playwright and Selenium end-to-end tests, Jest and React Testing Library, plus clean Jira tickets and pull requests.

aiWorkflow.title: AI-augmented development

standard.headline: Since 2026, working with AI has been the new standard.
standard.text: The way software gets built has changed. AI agents are now part of everyday development, and developers who don't use them are falling behind. I adapted quickly and rebuilt my day-to-day work around this new way of working. It's not a shortcut: it lets me deliver more, faster, to the same quality bar.

aiWorkflow.intro: Writing code is no longer the slow part. The slow parts are deciding what to build, checking that it's right, and shipping it safely. So I lead every step and use agents as my assistant across the whole delivery cycle: I set the direction, review every change and own what ships. I also know what AI gets wrong. I've rescued an app that AI had written badly, because I understood the frameworks underneath.

steps.title: Ticket
steps.me: I define the scope and acceptance criteria.
steps.agent: Creates and updates the Jira ticket through API / MCP integrations, with no manual clicking or CLI work.

steps.title: Analyse
steps.me: I decide what to investigate and verify the findings.
steps.agent: Reads the ticket, explores the codebase, and checks logs and failing jobs to find the root cause.

steps.title: Plan & branch
steps.me: I choose the direction and the trade-offs.
steps.agent: Lays out the options, then creates the branch for the agreed approach.

steps.title: Build
steps.me: I steer the implementation and keep the architecture clean.
steps.agent: Writes the code to the agreed plan and the project's conventions.

steps.title: Review & test
steps.me: I review every diff and check the result myself before anything moves on.
steps.agent: Writes and extends unit and Playwright tests.

steps.title: Pull request
steps.me: I sign off, teammates review, and we release.
steps.agent: Drafts the PR description and a first-pass code review.

steps.title: Document
steps.me: I decide what needs documenting, then edit for accuracy and publish.
steps.agent: Keeps the docs wiki current with Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern: code changes go in as sources, and the agent updates the pages, release notes and cross-links.

principles.title: Human in the loop
principles.description: The agent is my assistant, not my replacement. Nothing merges until I've read and understood it.

principles.title: Faster, same standards
principles.description: Shorter cycles from ticket to release, with tests, reviews and documentation kept in place.

principles.title: Framework knowledge first
principles.description: Agents are only as good as the person checking them. Knowing React, Vue and the platform underneath is how I catch what AI gets wrong.

experienceTimeline.shortDescription: React front-end development and QA on a reinsurance policy administration platform. I spotted that the project's documentation was scattered across standalone SharePoint files and replaced it with a documentation app that now covers 5 applications and 15 releases.

impactStory.headline: From scattered SharePoint files to docs for 5 apps and 15 releases
impactStory.gap: The project's documentation lived in standalone SharePoint documents. They were hard to find, quickly out of date and disconnected from the code that actually shipped, while the compliance department needed complete records.
impactStory.action: Nobody asked me to, but I saw the gap and built a documentation app on Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern: code changes and releases go in as sources, and AI agents keep an interlinked wiki current, with my review.
impactStory.result: It now covers 5 applications and 15 releases. Each application has dedicated pages for user and technical documentation, release notes, test results and the documents the compliance department requires.

highlights: Built a documentation app on Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern that replaced standalone SharePoint documents. It now covers 5 applications and 15 releases.
Each application has dedicated pages for user documentation, technical documentation, release notes, test results and compliance documentation, kept current by AI agents from code changes.
Build and fix React, Next.js and TypeScript screens on the shared component library, test manually and with Playwright, and fix front-end issues myself.
Write, refine and triage Jira tickets, and use AI agents across the delivery cycle with my review on every change.
experienceTimeline.longDescription: Pelagos is a reinsurance company. On its policy administration platform I work as a React front-end developer with QA responsibilities. Early on I noticed that the project's documentation was a set of standalone SharePoint documents: hard to find, quickly stale and disconnected from the code, while the compliance department needed complete, current records. I designed and built a documentation app based on Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern: code changes and releases are the raw sources, and AI agents maintain an interlinked wiki from them, with my review. It now covers 5 applications and 15 releases, and every application has dedicated pages for user documentation, technical documentation, release notes, test results and compliance documentation. Alongside that I build and fix React / Next.js screens, test the main journeys manually and with Playwright, and manage tickets in Jira.
experienceTimeline.challenge: Documentation for the platform existed only as standalone SharePoint files. Finding the right page was slow, content went stale with every release, and nothing connected the documents to what had actually shipped.
experienceTimeline.solution: I designed and built a documentation app on Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern. Code changes and releases go in as sources, and AI agents keep an interlinked wiki current, so each release adds its own documentation, release notes and test results. As a developer with QA responsibilities, I also fix the front-end issues I find myself.
experienceTimeline.impact: Documentation for 5 applications and 15 releases, each with user and technical docs, release notes, test results and compliance documents, in one place that stays current. It's easier and faster to use for me, the team, the client and the compliance department.
features: Documentation app built from scratch on Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern
User docs, technical docs, release notes, test results and compliance pages
React / Next.js screens and front-end fixes
experienceTimeline.parallelNote: In parallel with Proprio until Apr 2026

experienceTimeline.shortDescription: My employer since 2022: a software consultancy that embeds developers in international client teams. Through Sofomo I delivered projects for IQAir, Octopus, Proprio, FlexCare and TriplePoint, and contributed to Sofomo's own website.
highlights: Embedded in client teams across e-commerce, healthcare, education, ERP and insurance, often on two or three client projects in parallel.
Picked up a new stack and codebase quickly on each engagement: React, Vue, Next.js, Remix, Shopify Hydrogen, NetSuite and Salesforce.
Contributed to the company's Next.js corporate website with responsive, accessible components and SEO and performance work.
experienceTimeline.longDescription: Sofomo is a software consultancy company based in Poland that provides development services to international clients. As my employer since March 2022, Sofomo assigns me to client projects where I work as an embedded team member. I also contributed to the development and maintenance of the company's corporate website using Next.js and React, delivering responsive, accessible UI components and supporting SEO and performance improvements. The client engagements in my timeline (IQAir, Octopus, Proprio, FlexCare, TriplePoint) are through Sofomo.
experienceTimeline.challenge: Working as a consultancy developer means adapting quickly to different tech stacks, codebases and team dynamics while keeping delivery standards high on every client project.
experienceTimeline.solution: I kept consistent coding standards across projects and built hands-on expertise in multiple frameworks (React, Vue, Next.js, Remix) so I could contribute from the first weeks of each engagement.
experienceTimeline.impact: Delivered client projects across several industries (e-commerce, healthcare, education, ERP) while staying with the same employer long term.

experienceTimeline.shortDescription: My first client project. Besides writing the full Selenium test suite, I built a standalone Next.js app connected to the Jenkins API, so non-technical users could choose which features to test, run the tests themselves and read the results.

impactStory.headline: A self-service test runner for non-technical users
impactStory.gap: The client wanted non-technical people to run automated tests on chosen features, switching areas on and off, without a terminal or developer knowledge.
impactStory.action: I wrote all the Selenium test scenarios in their own repository, automated periodic runs in Jenkins, and built a standalone Next.js / React app on the Jenkins API to select, trigger and present test runs.
impactStory.result: Non-technical users could run exactly the tests they needed and see the results themselves, with no developer in the loop and no manual QA coordination.

highlights: Wrote all Selenium (Java) test scenarios for a Salesforce-based application, kept in an independent repository separate from the application code.
Automated periodic test runs in Jenkins.
Built a standalone Next.js / React app connected to the Jenkins API, where non-technical users switch features on or off, trigger runs and read the results.
experienceTimeline.longDescription: TriplePoint was my first client project. The goal was test automation for an internal Salesforce-based application, with one unusual requirement: non-technical people on the client side had to be able to run the tests for the features they cared about (switching areas on and off) without a terminal or any developer knowledge. I wrote all the Selenium test scenarios, kept them in a standalone repository independent from the application code, and automated periodic runs in Jenkins. Because Jenkins exposes an API, I built a dedicated Next.js / React application on top of it to select features, trigger runs and present results in a simple interface.
experienceTimeline.challenge: The client wanted non-technical users to choose which features to test and run automated tests on demand, without a terminal, without developer knowledge and without waiting for QA.
experienceTimeline.solution: I wrote the complete Selenium test suite in its own repository, scheduled automatic periodic runs in Jenkins, and built a standalone Next.js / React app connected to the Jenkins API so users could switch features on or off, trigger runs and read the results.
experienceTimeline.impact: Testing became self-service. Non-technical users ran exactly what they needed and saw the results immediately, and the team stopped coordinating test runs by hand.
features: Next.js app on the Jenkins API
Feature on/off selection for test runs

experienceTimeline.shortDescription: Joined a team of 6 as a front-end developer to extend an existing Vue app for a US healthcare staffing company. I saw it had been built as a single page with no real routing, defined what had to change, and became the Lead Front-end Developer who set the team's SPA architecture.

impactStory.headline: From a one-page Vue app to a proper SPA, and from developer to lead
impactStory.gap: I joined to help extend an existing Vue app. It had been built as a single page with no real routing, nowhere near the single-page-application standard the product needed.
impactStory.action: I mapped what had been built against what the product required, defined the changes, and set the standard for SPA structure, advanced routing and the front-end architecture as a whole.
impactStory.result: I became Lead Front-end Developer for the team of 6, and the app got a scalable architecture the team could build on.

highlights: Identified that the existing Vue app was built as a single page without proper routing, and defined what had to change.
Became Lead Front-end Developer in a team of 6, and set the standard for SPA structure, advanced routing and front-end architecture.
Delivered time-tracking and CRM workflow interfaces embedded in NetSuite for a US healthcare staffing company.
experienceTimeline.longDescription: FlexCare is a US healthcare staffing company. I joined the team as a front-end developer to help develop an existing Vue application deployed inside NetSuite for time tracking and internal CRM workflows. When I compared what had been built with what the product needed, I saw the problem: the app was effectively one page, with no proper routing or structure, far from the single-page-application standard it needed. I identified what had to change, and I became the Lead Front-end Developer who set the SPA structure, the routing approach and the front-end architecture for the team.
experienceTimeline.challenge: The existing Vue app had been built as a single page without proper routing or structure. It could not support the features the product needed, and adding more on top would only have made it worse.
experienceTimeline.solution: I analysed the current app against the requirements, defined the target single-page-application structure with advanced routing, and led the team in moving to that architecture while delivering the time-tracking and CRM workflows.
experienceTimeline.impact: The team of 6 got a scalable front-end architecture and clear standards to build on, and I stepped up from developer to Lead Front-end Developer.
features: Audit of the existing Vue app
Front-end architecture standards for the team
Time tracking and CRM workflow UIs

experienceTimeline.shortDescription: React, Vue and NetSuite, all used daily. The app had first been generated with AI by a non-technical client and didn't work. I fixed what AI had broken, made it production-ready and covered every area the client needed, including my own SuiteScript.

impactStory.headline: Rescuing an AI-generated app with real framework knowledge
impactStory.gap: The client, who wasn't technical, had first built the app with AI. It looked like an app, but it didn't work, and nobody on their side could tell why.
impactStory.action: Because I know React, Vue and NetSuite, I could see what AI had got wrong. I fixed it, connected the front end properly to the NetSuite platform, and wrote my own SuiteScript where needed.
impactStory.result: A working, maintainable product, with one developer covering every area the client needed: React, Vue and NetSuite.

highlights: Took over an app first generated with AI by a non-technical client, fixed what AI had broken and made it work in production.
Worked daily across React, Vue and NetSuite, covering every front-end area the client needed.
Wrote my own SuiteScript, and used my NetSuite knowledge to connect the front end with the platform, work faster and troubleshoot issues.
experienceTimeline.longDescription: Proprio needed front-end modules that extend native NetSuite ERP workflows for US-based operations. The application had first been built with AI by a non-technical client, and it didn't work. Because I knew the frameworks underneath, I could see where the generated code was wrong, fix it and make the application work. I worked daily across React, Vue and NetSuite, so I could cover every area the client needed. I even wrote my own SuiteScript. Understanding NetSuite helped me connect the front end with the platform properly, move faster and troubleshoot a lot of issues.
experienceTimeline.challenge: The first version of the app had been generated with AI by a non-technical client. It didn't work, it was hard to reason about, and it had to run inside NetSuite's deployment and integration constraints.
experienceTimeline.solution: I found and fixed what AI had broken, restructured the React and Vue modules, wrote SuiteScript where the platform needed it, and connected the front end properly to NetSuite.
experienceTimeline.impact: The client got a working, maintainable product, and one developer able to cover React, Vue and NetSuite. It's a real-world example of why AI-generated code still needs someone who understands the frameworks.
features: React and Vue modules inside NetSuite
Front end connected properly to the NetSuite platform
Troubleshooting across front end and platform

experienceTimeline.shortDescription: React developer in the team building IQAir's headless Shopify storefront with Remix and Hydrogen. My special contribution was translating Liquid theme code into React and learning how the Shopify platform and its APIs work.

impactStory.headline: Translating Shopify Liquid into React for a headless storefront
impactStory.gap: The store's behaviour lived in Liquid templates, and the new headless storefront needed the same behaviour in React, built on Shopify's APIs.
impactStory.action: Working in the team, I translated Liquid code into reusable React components on Remix and Hydrogen and learned how the Shopify platform and its APIs work.
impactStory.result: A production headless storefront for a global brand, and hands-on Shopify and e-commerce knowledge I can bring to the next team.

highlights: Translated Liquid theme code into reusable, typed React components for a headless storefront built on Remix and Shopify Hydrogen.
Learned the Shopify platform and its APIs in depth: real e-commerce experience I can bring to the next team.
Worked in the team on performance, SEO-friendly routing, and unit and component tests with React Testing Library.
experienceTimeline.longDescription: IQAir moved its e-commerce storefront to a headless Shopify setup, built in close cooperation with Shopify. I joined as a React developer working in the team. What was special about this project was translating the existing Liquid theme code into React components on Remix and Shopify Hydrogen, which meant learning how the Shopify platform and its APIs work. Alongside that, I contributed to performance, SEO-friendly routing, and unit and component tests.
experienceTimeline.challenge: The store's logic and UI lived in Liquid templates. The headless storefront needed the same behaviour as typed, reusable React components on Shopify's APIs, without losing performance or SEO.
experienceTimeline.solution: I translated Liquid code into React components on Remix and Hydrogen, integrated Shopify APIs, and added unit and component tests to keep a fast-moving codebase stable.
experienceTimeline.impact: A production headless storefront for a global brand, plus practical Shopify platform and API knowledge that gives me an advantage on e-commerce projects.

experienceTimeline.shortDescription: Lead front-end developer on a side project: a Next.js and React UI for an online learning platform, written by hand before AI coding tools.
highlights: Led the front end of a Next.js and React learning platform as a side engagement alongside my main project.
Built the components and pages with Tailwind CSS, all hand-written before AI coding tools.
Owned code structure and reviews for the front end.
experienceTimeline.longDescription: Octopus is a Poland-based online learning platform. I was the Lead Front-end Developer on it as a side project alongside my main engagement. It was pure front-end work: building the components and pages in Next.js, React and Tailwind CSS and owning the front-end code structure. It was all written by hand, before AI coding tools became part of my workflow.
experienceTimeline.challenge: Deliver a consistent, responsive UI for a content-heavy learning platform as a side project, with limited time.
experienceTimeline.solution: Built the front end in Next.js and React with a reusable Tailwind-based component set and a clear code structure.
experienceTimeline.impact: A working, consistent front end for the platform, and more lead experience.

experienceTimeline.shortDescription: Commercial website for a beauty salon, built in React with styled-components. One of my first client projects.
highlights: Designed and built a complete commercial website for a real client, end to end.
Responsive React UI with styled-components and SCSS.
experienceTimeline.longDescription: BeautyLash was one of my first commercial front-end projects, created before starting my professional career. It was a website for an eyelash beautician salon, designed to present services, pricing and contact information in a clean and visually appealing way. The project was built using React and styled-components, with a strong focus on layout, styling and responsiveness. The original site is no longer live, but a deployed version is available for preview.
experienceTimeline.challenge: Designing and implementing a complete commercial website independently while learning React and modern styling approaches.
experienceTimeline.solution: Built a React application using styled-components and SCSS, focusing on reusable components, consistent styling and a responsive layout tailored to the client's business needs.
experienceTimeline.impact: Delivered a fully functional commercial website for a real client, and gained hands-on experience with client communication and project ownership.

experienceTimeline.shortDescription: Fast, SEO-friendly business website built with Next.js and TypeScript for a gas heating installer, deployed on Vercel.
highlights: Built and deployed a production Next.js and TypeScript site on Vercel.
SEO-friendly structure, fast load times and a clear presentation of services.
experienceTimeline.longDescription: AS Serwis is a modern business website created for a gas heating devices installer. The project focused on clarity, performance and trust-building for a service-oriented business. Built with Next.js and TypeScript, the site emphasizes fast load times, an SEO-friendly structure and maintainable styling using CSS Modules. It is deployed on Vercel and designed to be easy to extend as the business grows.
experienceTimeline.challenge: Creating a professional, trustworthy online presence for a technical service business while keeping performance high and the architecture clean.
experienceTimeline.solution: Implemented a Next.js application with TypeScript and CSS Modules, focusing on semantic structure, responsive design and SEO best practices. Deployed on Vercel for reliability and fast delivery.
experienceTimeline.impact: A production-ready website that supports the business's visibility and builds client trust.

about.intro: React front-end developer with 5+ years building with React, Next.js, TypeScript and Vue, 4+ of them in commercial client teams, across headless Shopify e-commerce, NetSuite ERP extensions, healthcare CRM, an online learning platform and a reinsurance policy platform. Every project has needed something different, and I've made a habit of finding what's missing and building it. Before tech, I spent 12+ years managing teams in international hospitality.
